meta.what: (18) Money Russia took from foreign companies leaving: exit contributions to the federal budget, value handed to Russian buyers through forced discounts, and assets seized without (full) payment, by company home country and year. (24) Profits/dividends that Russian-owned companies abroad remit to Russia, by host country, 2019-2026.
meta.units: EUR bn, nominal. Years 2021-2026; 2026 = Jan-Aug, not annualised. Profits series also 2019-2020. Each value {low, central, high} (~90%).

series.exit_contribution: Direct payment to the Russian budget ('voluntary contribution' required by the government sub-commission: 10% of value from Dec 2022, 15% from Oct 2023, 35% of the deal from Oct 2024). Totals from MinFin budget data; split by home country with the KSE exited-cohort key (from companies_all.json) plus Carlsberg explicitly in 2024. Pre-war level 0, so the whole amount is the change. Toward Russia.
series.discount_transfer: Value handed to Russian buyers by the mandatory discount (>=50%, >=60% from Oct 2024) or nominal-price sales. 2022 from a case list (no contributions yet); 2023-2026 = contribution x d/c ratio; 2024 adds Yandex and Polymetal explicitly. A transfer to Russian residents, not to the state: kept separate so the builder can choose. Toward Russia if counted.
series.seizure: Asset value lost by the foreign owner minus consideration actually received abroad, in the year control was lost: decrees on temporary management, expropriations, court seizures tied to sanctions-cancelled contracts, leased aircraft kept by Russian airlines. A gain to Russia (state or Russian firms) and a loss to the company. Toward Russia if counted.
series.profits_remitted: Dividends/profits remitted to Russian parents by operating subsidiaries abroad (host country = where the subsidiary operates; holding conduits such as Cyprus, Austria's Lukoil International GmbH, Netherlands holdings and Swiss/UAE trading arms are not hosts). Level per year.
series.profits_change_vs_prewar: profits_remitted minus the 2019-2021 average (x 8/12 for 2026). Positive = more money to Russia than before the war (toward Russia), negative = less (toward Ukraine, where the host's own choice such as trusteeship or sanctions caused it).

budget_line_totals_rub_bn.note: Line 'non-government unrequited receipts / voluntary contributions'. 2025 includes some and 2026 mostly Russian business donations; MinFin said ~120bn arrived from exit sales in Jan-Mar 2025; Q1 2026 = 15.6bn.

russia_bop_direct_investment_income_cred.note: Bank of Russia BoP: all direct investment income receivable (incl. reinvested earnings and round-tripping via Cyprus etc.). Upper bound / cross-check only; not split by country after 2021.

overlaps: companies_all.json / round4a.json (company taxes): those count taxes paid by Russian subsidiaries while foreign-owned (profit tax + half of other taxes). KSE's 'all taxes' list mentions 'exit taxes' among other taxes; the voluntary exit contribution is normally paid by the seller or buyer to the budget, not by the subsidiary, so little of it should sit in KSE subsidiary tax data; if the builder adds exit_contribution, the worst case double count is half of at most EUR 1.6bn a year (the 'half of other taxes' weight), and the safe choice is to keep companies_all as is and add exit_contribution in full. Dividends that foreign companies still in Russia cannot repatriate (type-C accounts, BP's Rosneft dividends, RBI's EUR 4.4bn excess capital) are NOT counted here. Seizure values are asset values, not taxes, and do not overlap. Discount transfer and seizure are not payments to the Russian state and are not in any other file. Profits remitted (24): no other research file counts income on Russian outward FDI; Litasco/Swiss-UAE trading margins and Cyprus/Netherlands holding income are left out because they are part of Russian export revenue (already in trade/energy) or round-tripping. Lukoil's ISAB, NIS and Lukoil International sale prices are capital, not income, and are not counted.
notes: Exit payments are one-off; pre-war level is 0, so the series equal the change. 2026 exit share of the voluntary-contribution line is a guess (Q1 2026 15.6bn total before Russian business donations surged). Country split of contributions and of the 2023-2026 discount uses the KSE exited-cohort key derived from companies_all.json (weight of firms that sold out in 2023-2024) - certainty C/D for countries. Seizures are counted in the year the owner lost control. Aircraft: ~USD 10bn stranded minus >USD 2.5-3.5bn paid by Russian insurer NSK, net in 2022; Western insurer payouts to lessors shift the loss between Western countries but do not change Russia's gain. Profits remitted are mostly educated guesses built from Lukoil's 2021 outside-Russia EBITDA (RUB 281bn ~ EUR 3.2bn), typical net/EBITDA ~0.5 and payout 0.5-0.8, spread over hosts by asset size; NIS (Serbia) is from reported dividends. Russian BoP direct-investment income receivable fell from USD 35/29/66bn (2019-21) to 24/18/8/8bn (2022-25), but most of it is round-tripping through Cyprus etc. and cannot be split by host after 2021.
